title: The sandbox image's ARG TARGETARCH=amd64 makes every arm64 build fetch amd64 binaries
description:
cloud/sandbox/Dockerfile declares:

    ARG TARGETARCH=amd64

A DEFAULT on TARGETARCH shadows the value BuildKit supplies, so every arch-selected download in the image resolves to amd64 no matter what --platform asks for. Go, uv, bun, mise and omp are all fetched by that variable. An arm64 build of this image today is an arm64 base full of amd64 binaries.

Measured on docker 29.4.0 while implementing ticfac's prs:

    stage declares            COPY blob-linux- with --platform linux/arm64
    ARG TARGETARCH=amd64      blob-linux-amd64    WRONG
    ARG TARGETARCH            blob-linux-arm64    right

The fix is to declare it BARE - 'ARG TARGETARCH' - in every stage that uses it. A default is what breaks it; BuildKit always supplies a value, so there is nothing to default for.

Invisible in practice today because the factory builds amd64, which is why it has survived. It would bite the first time anyone builds this image for arm64 - including a developer on an Apple Silicon machine running a plain 'docker build', which defaults to the host platform.

Found by the agent implementing ticfac tick prs, which needed TARGETARCH for its own COPY and tested the behaviour rather than assuming it. ticfac cannot fix this: image/ is ticfac's vendored copy of this tree and ticfac never edits it.
acceptance_criteria: Every stage that reads TARGETARCH declares it bare, and an arm64 build of the sandbox image contains arm64 binaries for Go, uv, bun, mise and omp
